split_rationale: Karachi is served by a vertically-integrated private utility with its own generation and a limited NTDC interconnection - the reason it is a zone of its own rather than part of PAK_S.
model_plants: Bin Qasim, Port Qasim, Korangi, KESC units

split_rationale: Import delivery node, not a generating area: the model gives it zero capacity and only a transfer limit. The polygon is the north-east provinces served by that corridor and by CASA-1000.
grid_area: NEPS import node from Tajikistan (Sherkhan Bandar 220 kV)

split_rationale: Sughd is separated from the rest of Tajikistan by the Zarafshan range and was fed from the Central Asian ring through Uzbekistan; the South-North 500 kV line closed the gap but remains a modelled constraint.
Import delivery node with no generation; the Hairatan line is Kabul's single largest supply. Polygon = the provinces on that corridor.
grid_area: NEPS import node from Uzbekistan (Hairatan 220 kV)

split_rationale: Import delivery node with no generation, on the north-western Turkmen feeds.
grid_area: NEPS import node from Turkmenistan (Andkhoy / Sheberghan)

split_rationale: Herat is not synchronised with the rest of Afghanistan: it is a separate island fed from Iran (Islam Qala) and Turkmenistan, with Salma dam as its only local plant - hence its own zone.
Hydro-rich half: the Toktogul cascade and the Datka hub that exports to Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.
Holds the Vakhsh cascade and the national load centre, and is the export node towards Afghanistan and Pakistan (CASA-1000).
Before the Datka-Kemin 500 kV line the Kyrgyz north could only reach the southern cascade through Kazakh and Uzbek networks; the model keeps the two halves as separate nodes with an internal limit.
caveat: Kambarata-2 sits in Jalal-Abad (territorially KGZ_S) but feeds the northern 500 kV corridor, so the model dispatches it in KGZ_N. The polygon follows territory, not this single plant.

split_rationale: The only Afghan zone with its own generation: the Kabul river plants and Kajaki. Everything the country imports is delivered to it through the four border nodes below.
model_plants: Tarakhil, Naghlu, Sorobi, Darunta, Mahipar, Kajaki, Pul-e-Khumri
caveat: Kandahar, Helmand, Uruzgan and Zabul are physically the separate SEPS island, but the 2020 model carries a single domestic Afghan zone and dispatches Kajaki (Helmand, which supplies SEPS) in it, so they are folded in here. Within the polygon, provinces served only by isolated micro-grids are covered by approximation.

split_rationale: Pakistan's system is one long north-south chain. The hydro north and the thermal south are separated by the Guddu / Muzaffargarh transfer bottleneck, which is what the PAK_N-PAK_S link represents.
model_plants: Tarbela, Diamer-Basha, Dasu, Ghazi-Barotha, Mangla, Neelum-Jhelum, Chashma, Muzaffargarh, Kot Addu, Faisalabad, Balloki

split_rationale: Thermal and coal south (Sindh + Balochistan) minus the Karachi utility territory, which is a separate control area.
model_plants: Guddu, Uch, Jamshoro, Thar, Qadirpur, Karachi-Coastal, Sahiwal
caveat: Sahiwal coal is in Punjab territorially but is dispatched in PAK_S by the model. The polygon follows territory.

split_rationale: Single meshed national system - no internal constraint is represented.
model_plants: Syrdarya, Tashkent, Novo-Angren, Navoi, Talimarjan, Charvak, Fergana

split_rationale: Single national system; modelled as one node, exporting to Afghanistan and Iran. (Zone code TUR is the model's label for Turkmenistan - the ISO3 is TKM.)
model_plants: Mary, Ahal, Derweze, Balkanabat, Turkmenbashi, Dashoguz, Lebap

split_rationale: Deficit zone around Almaty and Shymkent, historically supplied through the Central Asian ring (Uzbekistan / Kyrgyzstan) and by the North-South transit; modelled separately because that transit is the binding limit.
model_plants: Balkhash-Ulken, Zhambyl GRES, Almaty CHPs, Kapchagay, Moynak, Chimkent, Shardara

split_rationale: Kazakhstan's UPS is three weakly-coupled zones. The Northern zone is the coal belt synchronised with Russia; it is linked to the South only by the North-South 500 kV transit, which is the constraint the model represents as the KAZ_N-KAZ_S corridor.
model_plants: Ekibastuz GRES-1/2, Aksu, Karaganda, Petropavlovsk, Ust-Kamenogorsk
